name: 220. Compressed request bodies may only expand in proportion to what was sent (decompression-expansion)
description: Request decompression runs ahead of routing and auth for anyone who can reach the listener. A body may expand to at most 100 times its compressed size, with a 1 MiB floor and the configured cap as the ceiling, and buffered decompressions charge the bytes they actually inflate to a process-wide budget of four times the cap (that concurrent requests are not refused is pinned by TestRequestDecompressionMiddleware_ConcurrentMultiMBGzipNotRefused, since the harness sends requests one at a time). The fixture is the gzip of 2 MiB of zeros, about two kilobytes on the wire, posted with no credential: it is answered 413 naming the expansion bound before the route or auth sees it, and the gateway keeps serving. Red before the change: the 2 MiB was inflated under the 100 MiB cap and the request reached auth, answering 401. The fixture file keeps the exact bytes on the wire; the openai keyword is only the harness filter label, no provider is called.
